module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-controlled UART that stores control settings, selects a baud tick from clkgen_i, queues transmit bytes through a TX FIFO, samples received bits into an RX path and FIFO, and drives serial, flow-control, interrupt, and bus-response outputs.

use-case flows.value: UART control settings written into held registers: enable, simulation mode, hardware flow control, prescaler, baud divisor, interrupt enables, and FIFO-clear commands
bus write request that enqueues a transmit byte into the TX FIFO interface
selected UART timing tick and baud reload values that pace transmit and receive bit processing
transmit frame loading and serialization to uart_txd_o
receive-bit sampling, frame assembly, and RX-FIFO write on completed byte reception
hardware flow control: sampled CTS can hold transmission, and RTS reflects enable and RX-half-full state
TX and RX interrupt requests generated from configured interrupt enables and FIFO status
receive overrun status set when a received byte arrives while the RX FIFO is full
stored control/status bits and received RX data returned on bus_rsp_o.data, with RX dequeue on data-register read
control registers, IRQ outputs, TX/RX engine state, overrun flag, and RTS output forced to reset values; FIFO clear controls also assert on disable or explicit clear

conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.enable is written at line 179 and held until reset or rewrite (lines 156,179). The module copies it to clkgen_en_o (line 228), forces both FIFO clear controls when low (lines 259,304), gates both interrupt outputs (lines 270,315), and injects it into the TX and RX engine state words (lines 344,417). These implemented flows make the enabled/disabled operating state an Integrity asset; availability is also established because the state is preserved between writes.

conceptual assets.concept: UART baud and prescaler timing configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.prsc and ctrl.baud are written at lines 182-183 and held in registers. ctrl.prsc selects uart_clk from clkgen_i at line 229, and ctrl.baud reloads the TX and RX baud counters at lines 349, 368, 422, and 432. Serial transmit and receive timing therefore depends on this configuration, establishing Integrity and availability of the timing state.

conceptual assets.concept: Hardware flow-control state between this UART and its peer
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.hwfc_en is configured at line 181. uart_ctsn_i is sampled into tx_engine.cts at line 337, and when hardware flow control is enabled the transmitter advances only if CTS permits it at lines 358-360. The same mode controls uart_rtsn_o at lines 472-480 together with the local enable and RX-half-full condition. This establishes Integrity of the consumed CTS state, the stored flow-control state, and the reported RTS output; availability applies under the RTL-visible conditions.

ctrl.clr_tx is a one-cycle stored command: it is cleared each cycle at line 174, set from the control write bit at line 191, and contributes to tx_fifo.clear at line 259, which is delivered to tx_engine_fifo_inst.clear_i at line 246. Because this decision discards or preserves queued transmit bytes, its Integrity and availability are established by the implemented clear flow.

ctrl.clr_rx is a one-cycle stored command: it is cleared each cycle at line 173, set from the control write bit at line 190, and contributes to rx_fifo.clear at line 304, which is delivered to rx_engine_fifo_inst.clear_i at line 291. Because this decision discards or preserves queued received bytes, its Integrity and availability are established by the implemented clear flow.

tx_fifo.we is asserted only for a bus strobe, write, and data-register address at line 261, and it is delivered to tx_engine_fifo_inst.we_i at line 251. The outgoing-data flow depends on this exact enqueue decision, so its Integrity is established; availability applies when those qualifying conditions hold.

tx_engine.sreg captures `tx_fifo.rdata & '0'` at line 351 and is shifted at lines 365-370; tx_engine.txd takes the current LSB at line 365, and uart_txd_o copies that bit at line 392. The transmit operation therefore depends on the integrity and availability of this stored frame and per-bit output. The earlier FIFO contents reside in the instantiated sub-unit and are not reportable here.

uart_rxd_i is sampled into rx_engine.sync at lines 408 and 410, shifted into rx_engine.sreg at lines 430-434, and completion is signaled by rx_engine.done at line 440 so the byte can be written to the RX FIFO at lines 305-306. The receive path depends on the exact captured bits and completion event, establishing Integrity and availability. The later bus readout exits only through the excluded transport record.

rx_fifo.re is asserted only for a bus strobe, read, and data-register address at line 307, and it is delivered to rx_engine_fifo_inst.re_i at line 299. This decision directly controls when stored received data is removed for readout, establishing Integrity and readout availability under the implemented conditions.

rx_engine.over clears on reset and when the UART is disabled (lines 456 and 459) and sets at lines 460-461 when a receive write occurs while the RX FIFO reports full. Status readback at line 214 depends on this flag, establishing Integrity and availability of the overflow indication.

ctrl.irq_tx_empty and ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf are stored at lines 188-189, and irq_tx_o is registered at lines 270-272 from ctrl.enable plus the selected TX FIFO status conditions. External interrupt delivery therefore depends on both the stored policy and the reported output, establishing Integrity; availability applies on cycles where the configured condition is true.

ctrl.irq_rx_nempty, ctrl.irq_rx_half, and ctrl.irq_rx_full are stored at lines 185-187, and irq_rx_o is registered at lines 315-318 from ctrl.enable plus the selected RX FIFO status conditions. This makes the configured receive-interrupt policy and the resulting output an Integrity asset; availability applies on cycles where the configured condition is true.
